chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying regarding the one who is unconscious (maghmā 'alayhi): 'That which Allah has caused to overcome him, then Allah is more worthy of excusing him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who is unconscious regarding missed prayers?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of divine exemption (ʿudhr) for those overcome by states beyond their control, such as unconsciousness. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that Allah’s will in imposing a condition is intrinsically linked to His mercy in relieving the individual of corresponding obligations, reflecting the broader theological concept of 'no burden beyond capacity.'

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws,
‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the unconscious: ‘What Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Caused to overcome upon him, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the closest with the Excusing’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say about one fainted because of illness, ‘Whomever Allah overpowers, Allah is the first to pardon.’”
